units.title: resume, LinkedIn profile, recruiters, linkedin, keywords, ATS
units.summary: Referrals are the social proof that tells recruiters you have worked with former colleagues. A good LinkedIn profile photo checks: smiling, looking at camera, alone, dressed professionally, not a selfie, no distracting background, decent lighting. It is recommended to aim for three or four recommendations before stopping. Ensure LinkedIn profile is up to date and GitHub profile is well organized.

units.title: amy, linkedin algorithm, linkedin headline, LinkedIn Legend, app, content
units.summary: LinkedIn Legend contains dozens of pre-designed LinkedIn banners, hundreds of headline phrases, 10 plus highly diverse about statement templates, and tons of effective icebreaker scripts, networking scripts, and content. The LinkedIn playbook has a full section on creating content. LinkedIn detects and suppresses authenticity, engagement pods, automation tools, and manufactured reactions. In 2026, your profile is the first signal the algorithm reads before deciding whether your content is worth distributing to anyone.

units.title: companies, speaker, Open to Work banner, work summary, LeetCode, notion
units.summary: The Open to Work banner presents risks to the user. Proactive outreach is preferable to using the Open to Work banner. There is debate about the advantages of using Open to Work. Relevant coursework could be cool and probably doesn't hurt to add, but only for internships.

units.title: AI, design system, components, design tokens, dashboard, landing page
units.summary: Your tech resume is garbage. This resume template minimizes vertical whitespace. The landing page converts visitors into buyers. My resume was good enough to get me into my dream job at Google.

units.title: Darwin, Sydney, brisbane, Melbourne, Perth, Adelaide
units.summary: If you follow my instructions, you are going to get a lot of interviews. Only about 2% to 5% of people who apply to a job will ever get an interview. Résumé templates need to be ATS optimized for 2026. Your LinkedIn profile is your personal storefront, and first impressions impact professional opportunities.

units.title: AI engineer, AI engineering, rag, LLM, prompt engineering, data scientist
units.summary: The job market is tough for software engineers, so resumes must be on point. You must take ownership of ambiguous problems and drive them from ideation to solution without waiting for instructions. LLMs like ChatGPT or Gemini can aid in your research. Many software engineers make resume mistakes without realizing it.

rubrics.criterion: Keep the resume to a single page.
rubrics.check: Count the pages of the final resume; if it goes past one page, it fails.
rubrics.why: Recruiters spend only about 7 seconds per resume, so extra pages lose attention and get the resume discarded.

rubrics.criterion: Include the exact keywords a recruiter would use to search for your target role in your resume and LinkedIn profile.
rubrics.check: Take the core terms from the target job posting or recruiter search (job title, required technologies, skills) and search the artifact for each; every core term must appear verbatim at least once.
rubrics.why: Recruiters and ATS systems find candidates by exact search terms, and profiles that lack those terms stay hidden from search results.

rubrics.criterion: Write a LinkedIn headline that includes your target role or search keywords, not just your current job title.
rubrics.check: Inspect the headline field; fail if it is blank, contains only a default 'Job Title at Company', or has no terms beyond the current position.
rubrics.why: A default or empty headline hides the profile from recruiter search, while a descriptive headline attracts recruiters to the profile.

rubrics.why: Recommendations are social proof, and recruiters check referrals before reaching out to a candidate.

rubrics.criterion: If you use LinkedIn's Open to Work feature, set its visibility to recruiters only rather than broadcasting it to your whole network.
rubrics.check: Open the Open to Work settings and confirm the audience option is restricted to recruiters; a public green Open to Work frame or an 'all LinkedIn members' visibility setting fails.
rubrics.why: Publicly advertising that you need a job lets employers know you are unemployed and can weaken their offers; recruiters-only keeps the signal without that risk.

rubrics.why: Reviewers spend only a minute or two, and vertical whitespace on a resume is space that should carry information.

rubrics.criterion: Quantify every achievement with a concrete numeric metric; when the raw number is confidential, express the same impact as a percentage or multiplier.

rubrics.why: Numbers show you know the details of the work and make the result intuitive for a recruiter; if real metrics are proprietary, percentages or multipliers preserve impact without leaking confidential data.

rubrics.criterion: Name the specific technologies, frameworks, and tools used to achieve each result instead of describing the outcome in general terms.

rubrics.why: A claim on its own says little about what the candidate actually did; naming the tools demonstrates the technical skill and makes the achievement credible and easy to understand.
